summary: Session-resume surge from tenant causing upstream restarts and elevated 5xx across private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
A Brightline Health tenant observed a sudden increase in 5xx errors from the API gateway for streaming and short request workloads. Error rate spike began ~2026-03-12 03:07 UTC and affected ~12% of the customer's requests for ~40 minutes. Support escalation requested due to degraded user-facing experience in production.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: end users experienced failed streams and short-text generation failures (5xx).
- Scope: single private deployment (Brightline Health VPC) in us-west-2, multiple routes across streaming and standard generation.
- Business: client escalation with account team; potential SLA credit if unresolved.

Observed behavior:
- API gateway returned a mix of 502/503/504 to client SDKs.
- Upstream runtime processes for the tenant showed repeated restarts and a short crash loop during the window.
- Error pattern correlated with a very high rate of TLS session resumption attempts (session-ticket and session-id churn) from a small fleet of customer IPs.

Required action: triage with SRE to identify whether root cause is networking (conn churn), runtime memory pressure, or recent runtime/kernel changes.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Send sustained short streaming requests (1-3 token responses, keepalive disabled) from a small number (~20) of concurrent clients, with clients rapidly reconnecting and requesting TLS session resumption instead of full handshakes.
2) Observe edge logs for session-cache misses and connection churn.
3) Watch private runtime logs for elevated prefetch activity and abrupt worker restarts.

Notes: reproduction requires session-resume behavior; normal long-lived keepalives do not trigger the same amplification.
logs_snippets:
[2026-03-12T03:07:12Z] apigw-usw2-01: http2: stream reset by peer (RST_STREAM) - tenant=brightline
[2026-03-12T03:07:13Z] runtime-tenant-172: Unhandled signal: SIGABRT (runtime-worker) - pid=8421 - reason=GPU memory alloc failed while loading shard
[2026-03-12T03:08:01Z] apigw-usw2-01: 502 Upstream connection closed prematurely - lat_p50=120ms lat_p99=2.1s
[2026-03-12T03:10:40Z] autoscaler: detected burst, attempted scale +2 workers but scale failed with insufficient capacity in private pool
investigation_notes:
Initial telemetry: session-resume attempts from 3 customer edge IPs spiked by ~8x at 03:07 UTC; connection churn increased accept_rate and short-lived TCP connections on the private gateway. Gateways retried failed backends which amplified load onto runtime prefetch code path. Around same time (03:06 UTC) we rolled a runtime kernel optimization (PR #993) in the us-west-2 private cluster that increased temporary GPU memory usage under heavy prefetch. Hypothesis: combination of resumption storm + increased transient memory footprint triggered GPU allocation failures -> worker exits -> gateway retries -> retry amplification -> elevated 5xx.

Supporting evidence:
- Correlation between session-resume spike and first worker exit timestamp.
- Kernel optimization increases temporary allocation shown in metrics (gpu_mem_temp_alloc 18% -> 62% under churn).
- No other tenants on the same host showed identical patterns (tenant-specific request pattern + model pinning).

Mitigations attempted during window:
- Rate-limited session accept on gateway for tenant (applied 03:12 UTC) -> error rate dropped by 70% within 6 minutes.
- Scaled private pool (attempted) but capacity constrained in that private cluster.
- Rolled back PR #993 from the private cluster for the tenant pool at 03:20 UTC -> runtime worker restarts stabilized.
resolution:
Workaround applied: temporarily disable session-resume acceptance for Brightline Health at the gateway and rolled back the recently deployed kernel optimization in the tenant's private pool. This removed the immediate 5xx spike and stabilized runtime workers.

Permanent follow-ups:
- Postmortem to validate root cause and sequence (owners: SRE Marco Li, Runtime Eng Priya Desai) due by 2026-03-19.
- Add a guardrail to the gateway to detect session-resume floods and apply early throttling per-tenant. (Owner: network team).
- Add a canary memory-pressure check to the kernel selection path so runtime kernel changes that increase transient memory usage require a canary with prefetch-heavy workload. (Owner: runtime team).
- Update Private deployment runbook with steps to force-evict/isolated fallback routing for misbehaving tenant sessions.

Customer communication: account team notified; Brightline confirmed they accepted temporary throttle while we implement long-term fixes.
